chunks: And it is narrated in another report:

If someone has intercourse at the beginning of the Month of Ramadan and then forgets the ghusl (ritual bath) until the Month of Ramadan ends, then he must perform ghusl and make up his salat (prayer) and sawm (fasting), unless he had performed ghusl for Jumu'ah, in which case he makes up his salat and fasting only up to that day and does not make up what comes after that.

key_terms.الْغُسْلَ: the ritual bath required after major ritual impurity
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the Month of Ramadan, during which fasting is obligatory
key_terms.لِلْجُمُعَةِ: for Friday, referring to the ghusl of Jumu'ah
key_terms.يَقْضِيَ: to make up missed acts of worship

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone forgets ghusl after intercourse in Ramadan until the month ends?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who remained in a state requiring ghusl after intercourse during Ramadan due to forgetfulness. It states that he must perform ghusl and make up affected prayers and fasts, but if he had later performed ghusl for Friday, the obligation of making up only extends until that day.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1896 - It is narrated in another report:

"If someone has intercourse at the beginning of the Month of Ramadan and then forgets to perform ghusl (ritual bathing) until the Month of Ramadan ends, he must perform ghusl and make up his prayers and fasts. However, if he performed ghusl for Jumu'ah (Friday prayer), then he only needs to make up his prayers and fasts up to that day and does not need to make up what comes after it."
